identity.real_world_identity_notes: The F-Inter MG-15, a purpose-built Brazilian single-seater constructed by Minelli Racing for the real Fórmula Inter category, which ran under FASP's Paulista championship. The record previously carried only an AMS2 sheet identity for the 2015-2023 entry; a launch report now names the model and its constructor. No reliable source expands "MG", so it is treated as part of the model designation and not as a person or a year.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection established the rim category and display, shift-light, and open-top details.

notes: Current guided AMS2 testing established move-off, running-shift technique, and cockpit controls with simulator assists disabled.
A clutch is required from rest.

The steering lock came from the AMS2 spreadsheet, which records what the simulator applies rather than what the real car was built with. It moves to the simulator layer, where that evidence belongs; no reviewed source establishes the real car's lock.

This record came from the original AMS2 spreadsheet import, where one claim covered the identity, the whole of authentic_controls and the simulator behaviour together. The car has since been driven, and the guided observation establishes those controls directly. The spreadsheet claim no longer reaches authentic_controls, because it describes what the simulator models and cannot settle what the real car had.

The category and the car are real, which was the first question asked of this record and the one that decided whether it survives. The F-Inter MG-15 was built by Minelli Racing for Fórmula Inter, a category FASP ran in its Paulista championship. This record does not retire as a simulator construction.

The gearbox was made in-category, and that narrows the routes to its construction rather than opening them. The launch report says it was "produzida pela própria equipe técnica da Fórmula Inter" with five ratios in an H. Because it names no donor production unit, the reasoning that settled Formula Vee - a sealed production gearbox is a road unit, therefore synchromesh - does not reach this car. No source uses "sincronizado" or "garras", so the construction is absent from the record rather than denied.

The regulation route is closed as far as published material goes. FASP's 2024 sporting regulation carries "ANEXO 5 - FÓRMULA INTER" on page 38, which proves the category but is a points table in full: no gearbox article, no prescribed, sealed or free rule, no ratios. No CBA, FASP or promoter technical regulation for the 2015-2023 MG-15 was located. This is a bounded negative finding rather than an unfinished search.

Two launch accounts disagree on ratio count: five in one, four in the other, both naming this car and its constructor. The record keeps five, which the guided drive established directly and which the more detailed account corroborates. No source explains the difference and it may be a prototype or a specification change, so it is recorded rather than resolved, and it is not read as evidence about the construction in either direction.

The dogleg gate has no real-world corroboration. Both launch accounts describe the gate only as an "H", which is generic and neither confirms nor denies a dogleg, and neither gives a first-gear position. The dogleg with first down and left remains observed in the simulator only.

Knowingly blocked on the downshift blip, recorded rather than carried quietly. The blip is `required` in authentic_controls on the strength of the guided drive, and a drive establishes what AMS2 demands rather than what the real car needed. Where the construction was later established for a car in this position - Formula Vee Gen2, Formula Vee FIN and the Diablo SV-R - the authentic value was revised to optional every time and the simulator's demand moved to an override. Three out of three. So this value is carried without corroboration and is more likely wrong than right; it stays because no source establishes the construction that would settle it, and the dataset does not convert a value by assumption.

What would unblock it: Minelli Racing's own documentation, or a technical regulation held somewhere the public web does not reach. The gearbox was made in-category with no donor production unit named, and FASP's annex for the category is a points table with no technical articles, so both routes tried are closed.
Guided current-game testing directly established all user-facing controls.

confidence.basis: Exact current-game identity, driving technique, and cockpit controls were directly tested through the guided workflow.

claims.basis: A 2015 launch report names the F-Inter MG-15 and its constructor, Minelli Racing, and establishes Fórmula Inter as a real Brazilian category, matching the simulator's telemetry name for this car. That replaces an identity held on a simulator spreadsheet alone. Short of verified because no source ties the simulator's model to a specific chassis or season within the 2015-2023 span, and two launch accounts disagree on the car's ratio count. Falsified by a source showing the MG-15 designation or the constructor to be something else, or by evidence that the simulator models a different Fórmula Inter car.

Reviewed guided observation of the exact AMS2 1.6.9.91 identity; draft hash 6352bdce. The guided drive observed the gate in the cockpit and reported an ordinary dogleg, with first down and to the left of the racing plane.

driver_summary: Dogleg gate - first is down and left, outside the racing plane, so second through fifth fall in one straight line. The gate was seen in the cockpit; no reviewed source establishes the real car's gearbox.

archetype.basis:
A dogleg archetype now exists and this car matches none, for a reason worth stating precisely. Its construction is unestablished, which alone would leave it deviating on a gap. What excludes it is the downshift blip, recorded as required - a known value, not a gap - where the archetype has it optional because a synchromesh does not need one to engage.

That is the dataset's own rule: required is reserved for gearboxes that need the blip. So this record asserts, through the blip, a construction its gearbox_type does not establish. Nine records were in that position. Four dissolved rather than resolved: they are cars a simulator invented, and a car with no real referent has no real gearbox to be wrong about, so the simulator's demand is the whole fact. This record is one of the five real cars where the tension stands, and it stands knowingly: the blip comes from a guided drive, and where the construction was later established for a car in this position the authentic value was revised to optional every time. Establishing the construction settles both fields at once.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "formula". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
